risks: Uses personal session cookies and likely violates Facebook terms of service
Lead-generation framing suggests bulk collection of personal data
Abandonment risk from reliance on undocumented internal endpoints

social-media.description: Open-source, local-first social media research agent for Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn. Jev routes read-only steps; socai CLI captures cited browser evidence.
social-media.summary: Local-first research agent that uses an LLM to choose read-only steps, such as searching, opening posts or profiles and reading comments on Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn. The socai CLI runs them in the user's signed-in Chrome and returns cited evidence for reports.
strengths: Local-first design with read-only operations and documented data flow
Produces source-cited reports with recorded example output
Open source with a tests badge and a stated release version
risks: Runs through the user's logged-in browser sessions, which raises platform terms and account-safety concerns
Profile and comment extraction could be used to build dossiers on individuals
Heavy reliance on a separate socai CLI and an OpenRouter key

social-media.summary: Rust CLI and HTTP service that inspects public GitHub profiles, repositories, commit identities and SSH keys, producing JSON, Markdown, text, SVG or PDF reports with source references and caveats about inferred data.
strengths: Clear documented modes (FAST and DEEP) and output formats
Privacy and limitations section and explicit distinction of observed vs inferred data
Does not execute code from inspected repositories
risks: Aggregates personal commit email addresses and activity timezone inferences about individuals
Optional GitLeak enrichment touches leaked-data sources

social-media.description: Instagram Scraper — free, open-source Instagram scraper. Unlimited profiles, posts, reels, comments and hashtags as clean JSON, no API key, no proxies.
social-media.summary: A Python API that scrapes public Instagram profiles, posts, reels, comments and hashtags into JSON, run locally via a FastAPI-style server with 19 endpoints. Marketed as free and unlimited.
strengths: Runnable local API with a curl example
Clear endpoint coverage for profiles, posts, comments and hashtags
Open-source and installable from requirements
risks: Scrapes personal profile data and email addresses, raising privacy concerns
Marketing claims of unlimited data without stated limits or legal considerations
Likely to break against Instagram changes; bundled promotional content

social-media.description: 🔮 Early access to the latest ASIMOV Alpha builds for agentic social media intelligence.
social-media.summary: Early-access alpha distribution of ASIMOV, an agent skill for social media intelligence. It claims to map social graphs from LinkedIn, X, Instagram, Luma and GitHub and enrich them with local CRM contacts. The README gives little detail on data sources, usage limits or legal cons
strengths: Clear focus on social media intelligence
Integrates with common AI agents as a skill
risks: Bypasses restrictive APIs for social platforms, raising terms-of-service concerns
Closed early-access distribution with little verifiable source code
Enriches public data with private contacts and CRM data

social-media.description: Self-hosted Telegram toolkit: comment collector, chat indexer, full-text search, audience overlap analytics and channel finder (Telethon + FastAPI + React, Docker)
social-media.summary: A self-hosted Telegram web panel (Telethon, FastAPI, React, Docker) that collects channel commenters, indexes group and forum history, runs full-text search, computes audience overlaps and maps people to their channels.
strengths: Clear, self-hosted design with data kept in one SQLite file
Documents features, inputs and outputs in detail
Full-text search, export to XLSX/CSV/JSON and scheduled monitoring
risks: Stores personal fields such as passport numbers and emails and computes suspicion scores on individuals
Uses a regular user account via MTProto, which may breach Telegram terms
Legal and ethical use of collected personal data is not clearly addressed in the excerpt

social-media.description: Export the complete follower list of any public X (Twitter) account to CSV + JSONL.
social-media.summary: Python CLI that uses a user's session cookies to call X's internal GraphQL API and export the full follower list of a public account to CSV and JSONL, with resume checkpoints and multi-session rotation.
strengths: Concrete usage examples and documented output files
Documents rate limits and resume checkpoint behaviour
Clear flags and maintenance notes for rotating queryIds
risks: Uses session cookies and README admits likely violation of X Terms of Service
Relies on undocumented internal API that may break
Bulk harvesting of follower profiles raises privacy concerns

social-media.description: Who's being heard, not just who's talking. Public social posts of candidates in the 2026 Czech municipal elections across ten cities, collected with Apify into a DuckDB evidence graph and mapped in a static app.
social-media.summary: Starwatch maps public social media posts of 2026 Czech municipal election candidates across ten cities, collected via Apify into a DuckDB graph and shown in a static map app with engagement snapshots.
strengths: Clear methodology: independent ownership verification before attribution
Links every post back to its original source
Explicitly avoids polls and forecasts per Czech pre-election law
risks: Profiles public candidate social accounts, a caution-level person-tracking style of collection
Hackathon-origin project with a fixed snapshot rather than ongoing maintenance

social-media.description: Instagram OSINT Framework to extract public profiles, posts, reels, comments, mentions, hashtags, and places from Instagram using the Apify API. 🕵🏽‍♂️
social-media.summary: CLI tool that uses the Apify instagram-scraper API to collect public Instagram profiles, posts, reels, comments, mentions, hashtags and places, saving JSON and TXT reports with timestamps.
strengths: Clear CLI usage examples for each target type
Batch processing from TXT file and local timestamped reports
Lists dependencies and supported systems
risks: Profile scraping of individuals could enable social profile extraction
Relies on a third-party paid scraping service and API key
Disclaimer is generic; limited discussion of legal or platform-terms considerations

transport-sensor.description: Android Wi-Fi/BLE radar terminal with camera-maker, tracker, Flock and public safety signatures. Works alone or with an optional CYD over USB.
transport-sensor.summary: Android app that scans nearby Wi-Fi and Bluetooth signals, showing signal strength and matching manufacturer signatures for cameras, trackers, and public safety devices such as Flock Safety and Axon. Optionally pairs with an ESP32-based CYD board over USB for extra radio readings
strengths: Documents limits and false-positive caveats clearly
Published signed APK and firmware with verification docs
risks: Tracker and camera signatures could be used to locate individuals
Ethical framing centred on surveillance of law enforcement equipment

web-capture.description: A resumable desktop app for searching, downloading, and keyword-scanning public Wayback Machine captures with configurable CDX parameters.
web-capture.summary: A resumable desktop and CLI tool that indexes Wayback Machine captures via CDX, downloads and validates saved page bodies, scans them with chosen keyword sets, handles media discovery, and produces reports.
strengths: Resumable CDX indexing with checkpoints
Documented workflows with pacing and retry behaviour
Cross-platform desktop and CLI builds
risks: Large-scale archive crawling can strain the Internet Archive if misconfigured
README is long and partly unverified in detail

web-capture.description: Swiftel: a keyless Rust CLI for public web search, fetch, crawl, and evidence-aware research.
web-capture.summary: Swiftel is a keyless Rust command-line tool for public web research. It searches, fetches pages as text or Markdown with hashes, maps and crawls same-origin URLs, ranks excerpts, converts documents, and checks certificate-transparency and archive context.
strengths: Keyless operation with no hosted account or required paid API
Clear command table with described outputs and budgets for crawling
risks: Optional browser and AI planning features add scope beyond core OSINT
Crawling and fetching public sites raises robots and rate-limit compliance questions

web-capture.description: High-Performance Wayback Machine CDX Recon & Triage Workspace for Chrome (Manifest V3). Stream archived URLs, rank by security risk, verify live 200s, and export.
web-capture.summary: Chrome Manifest V3 extension that streams Wayback Machine CDX archived URLs, ranks them by security risk (.env, keys, .git, SQL dumps), mines parameters, verifies live 200s, and exports results.
strengths: Concrete features: streaming CDX parsing, risk tiers, live HEAD verification
Runs locally as an unpacked extension with clear install steps
Zero-tracking privacy stance stated
risks: Security-recon framing leans toward attack-surface work with bug-bounty and fuzzing emphasis
Some README claims are marketing-style (High-Performance, Zero Tracking badges)

web-capture.description: Rased (راصد) — Production-grade headless Chromium reconnaissance engine + interactive Web Playground: network interception, .meta asset mirroring & in-page JS telemetry.
web-capture.summary: Rased is a Python tool that drives a headless Playwright Chromium pool to capture network responses, JavaScript bundles and sourcemaps, mirror origin trees with JSON metadata sidecars, and evaluate JS in page context. It includes a CLI and a web playground.
strengths: Concrete CLI options for scope and MIME filtering
Mirrors assets with header and CSP telemetry in .meta sidecars
Has install steps and a quick start
risks: Active crawling of targets, which may be out of scope without permission
Framed mainly for bug bounty and AppSec rather than OSINT
Limited detail on legal considerations

web-capture.description: GOBLIN TSUNAMI - OSINT framework generating 400+ Google Dorks across Instagram, Threads, Facebook & TikTok. Advanced digital footprint analysis with 25+ tracking categories for cybersecurity professionals, threat intelligence, and ethical reconnaissance operations.
web-capture.summary: Python framework that generates large sets of Google dork queries targeting Instagram, Threads, Facebook and TikTok to map an individual's digital footprint across tracking categories. README is mostly marketing with little concrete usage detail.
strengths: Clear dork-generation purpose across four platforms
Install instructions provided
risks: Targets individuals' digital footprints, enabling person tracking and location profiling
Heavy marketing language with few concrete examples or limits
Placeholder links and repository URLs suggest unfinished project

web-capture.description: Kumpulan tools OSINT (IP Tracker & Google Dorking) berbasis Python untuk Termux.
web-capture.summary: A small Python toolkit for Termux with three scripts: a menu launcher, an automatic Google dorking tool with 20 categories, and an IP geolocation tracker. Installation steps are given, but the README offers little on usage detail, outputs, or limits.
strengths: Simple installation steps for Termux
Clear list of the three tools
risks: Little detail on outputs and limits
Google dorking automation may violate search provider terms

web-capture.description: Ferramenta de dorking em múltiplos motores de busca para coleta de URLs em operações de OSINT e reconhecimento.
web-capture.summary: SimpleReconDorking runs search dorks in parallel across multiple search engines and returns the union of found URLs. Supports dork strings, files, a built-in categorised catalogue, and stdin, with Docker install and usage examples.
strengths: Clear purpose and multiple input modes
Documented usage examples and Docker setup
Built-in dork catalogue by category
risks: Dorking can be used to find exposed targets; README carries a consent warning only
Some engines require browser bypass, which may violate terms of service

web-capture.summary: Python client that queries a CIRCL-hosted Common Crawl index service to search archived web pages by URL, hostname, FQDN or digest, and retrieves only the selected WARC byte ranges. Access requires a token issued by CIRCL on request.
strengths: Queries metadata index before fetching, avoiding full crawl downloads
Documents multiple search modes and output formats with examples
risks: Depends on a token-gated third-party service with discretionary access
Access controls and README sample commands are partially truncated

web-capture.description: Ferramenta de extração e descoberta de URLs para fluxos de OSINT e reconhecimento
web-capture.summary: Python CLI that takes seed URLs, fetches pages and passive/active sources to extract and discover reachable URLs, with optional same-origin spidering, recursive rounds, Docker support and API-key-based sources.
strengths: Clear purpose for URL discovery in recon workflows
Supports passive and active sources, crawling and Docker
Documents usage flags, profiles and presets
risks: Active probing of target sites may raise authorisation concerns
Readme digest shows template-like source examples, limited detail on data sources

workspace-analysis.description: Maltego OSINT for AI agents: MCP server with 20 tools, 30 transforms, Machines, investigation copilot and native .mtgx. npx -y mcp-maltego
workspace-analysis.summary: MCP server letting AI agents run Maltego-style OSINT transforms and Machines, build link graphs with investigation state, and export native .mtgx files for Maltego Desktop/CE, with many zero-key data sources.
strengths: Works with many MCP clients and runs free without commercial Maltego license
Lists concrete no-key data sources such as crt.sh, RDAP, URLhaus and CISA KEV
risks: Marketing-heavy README with superlatives like high-performance and all-in-one
Investigation of people via some transforms may raise privacy concerns

workspace-analysis.description: Watchdog (branding subject to change) is an open-source intelligence (OSINT) case management platform for small teams.
workspace-analysis.summary: Open-source case management platform for small OSINT teams. Lookup results are held as proposals that a person must accept before entering the case graph, with export regenerated from the graph. Pre-1.0.
strengths: Human-in-the-loop acceptance of machine results supports defensible provenance
Clear architecture and stack documentation with CI and coverage badges
risks: Pre-1.0 with schemas and API shapes changing without notice
Not hardened for multi-tenant or production deployment

workspace-analysis.description: Collaborative peer-to-peer OSINT investigation board — end-to-end encrypted, no server-side data, works offline. Desktop app for Windows & Linux.
workspace-analysis.summary: COSINT is an offline-capable, peer-to-peer desktop investigation board for Windows and Linux. Analysts map entities, link them, grade sources, and collaborate in real time with end-to-end encryption and no server-side storage.
strengths: Clear architecture with E2E encrypted P2P sync and no backend
Concrete features: entity taxonomy, Admiralty source grading, .trace export
Multilingual UI and offline and 100% local modes
risks: Mostly case-management tooling rather than data collection
Tests and badges are self-reported; no independent verification of claims

workspace-analysis.description: Local-first OSINT investigation workspace: entities, graph, timeline, map, canvas, sources and evidence in plain Markdown, with optional AI runtimes and a browser extension. Built on Tangent.
workspace-analysis.summary: A local-first desktop workspace (fork of Tangent) for OSINT investigations. Organises entities, graphs, timelines, maps, canvases, sources and evidence as Markdown and YAML files, with optional AI chat runtimes and a Chromium capture extension.
strengths: Local-first data stored in plain Markdown and YAML files
Bundled FollowTheMoney-shaped schemas and multiple views of the same records
Demo workspace with fictional case data and install guides
risks: Windows and Linux binaries are unsigned; users must verify SHA-256 digests
macOS has no supported binary yet
Depends on a fork of Tangent and some optional features are described only briefly

workspace-analysis.description: An OSINT investigation case mapping tool for organizing entities, relationships, evidence, and intelligence.
workspace-analysis.summary: A local, offline investigation case tool for profiling subjects, mapping link networks with shortest path and centrality, placing locations on a map, building timelines, storing evidence with an audit log, and exporting PDF or HTML reports.
strengths: Runs locally with no server or telemetry
Concrete features: link network analysis, timeline, evidence vault with audit log
Install options and sample case reports provided
risks: Subject profiling of individuals could be misused for personal data collection
Limited detail on data sources and legal considerations

workspace-analysis.description: Terminal-first local OSINT field workbench with rigorous evidence provenance. Cases, content-addressed evidence, origin clustering, contradiction candidates, honest tool catalogue. Local-first, no telemetry.
workspace-analysis.summary: Terminal-first local OSINT workbench that stores collected artifacts as hash-addressed evidence within scoped cases, tracks claims and relations, clusters origins, flags contradictions, and exports bundles verifiable with sha256sum.
strengths: Hash-addressed, re-verifiable evidence chain
Honest feature matrix and limitations documented
Local-first with no telemetry
risks: Alpha status (v0.1.0), pre-release
Username checks cover a small provider set

workspace-analysis.description: Research studio and evidence workspace: cases, provenance, provider adapters, web API and job-scoped worker architecture. Released source; operator configuration required.
workspace-analysis.summary: A local-first OSINT investigation studio with case management, provenance tracking, and geographic parcel collection from public ArcGIS cadastral sources, plus web discovery and technology fingerprinting with human review before export.
strengths: Case workspace with provenance and human review before export
Uses named public data source (Florida statewide cadastral FeatureServer)
Documents architecture and setup
risks: Parcel ownership collection could be used to profile private owners
Setup requires operator configuration; source released with limited detail on legal considerations
Sherlock and Shodan topics suggest account and device lookup capabilities

workspace-analysis.description: Offline desktop workspace for organizing OSINT investigations.
workspace-analysis.summary: OpenTrace is an offline Windows/Linux desktop app (PySide6) for organizing OSINT investigations with a visual board, tasks, sources, hypotheses, journal, SHA-256 integrity info, and portable case folders. No telemetry or accounts.
strengths: Fully offline with no telemetry or accounts
Visual investigation board with relationships and exports
Tests in CI on Windows and Ubuntu
risks: Early-stage project with limited documentation of data formats
Binary release targets Windows x64 only

workspace-analysis.description: Open source alternative of Palantir Gotham  🌟 Star if you like it! 🌟'
workspace-analysis.summary: Open-source intelligence integration and link-analysis platform meant as an alternative to Palantir Gotham, with ontology-driven data fusion, graph visualization, GIS mapping, timelines and an AI co-pilot. Much of the described functionality is planned rather than implemented.
strengths: Clear purpose as a Gotham-style analysis workspace
Backend and frontend setup steps given
risks: Heavy marketing language with little concrete detail on data sources
Many features listed as planned rather than working
Defense and law enforcement targeting without stated legal safeguards
